top_matched_solutions.evidence_text:
Udaipur is an amazing place! The way it's growing in 10 years it will enter the BLACKI club. You'll have an amazing time there. The admin is a little strict although, but you'll get the hang of it dw. 

887 with 30 months worked is a little above average profile, and that's only because of the gap. If you remove the gap, it's an amazing profile. So just start working on a good explanation for the Gap in your placement interviews and you'll be fine.

As far as SIPs are concerned, don't think so far ahead for now, focus on the hurdles infront of you. Getting there, induction week, getting the hang of the MBA curriculum. By the time you get adjusted to it, you won't even know that you're already halfway done with your SIP prep. 

Just one word of advice, do not take SIP rejections to your heart. Placement interviews aren't an exact science, and sometimes shortlists happen for the most random of reasons. So never be let down by it. Work on your CV, don't try and include everything in your CV, and always edit your CV before applying, making it customised for the role you're applying to.

All the best! <3

top_matched_solutions.post_title: IIM Sambalpur - AMA (Class of 2025 Grad)
top_matched_solutions.parent_context:
I am going to join Udaipur next month? How would you rate it? My profile is 8/8/7 30 months workex with 1.5 years of gap, is my profile bad/average/good? I am a gem btw.

top_matched_solutions.evidence_text:
Udaipur is an amazing place! The way it's growing in 10 years it will enter the BLACKI club. You'll have an amazing time there. The admin is a little strict although, but you'll get the hang of it dw. 

887 with 30 months worked is a little above average profile, and that's only because of the gap. If you remove the gap, it's an amazing profile. So just start working on a good explanation for the Gap in your placement interviews and you'll be fine.

As far as SIPs are concerned, don't think so far ahead for now, focus on the hurdles infront of you. Getting there, induction week, getting the hang of the MBA curriculum. By the time you get adjusted to it, you won't even know that you're already halfway done with your SIP prep. 

Just one word of advice, do not take SIP rejections to your heart. Placement interviews aren't an exact science, and sometimes shortlists happen for the most random of reasons. So never be let down by it. Work on your CV, don't try and include everything in your CV, and always edit your CV before applying, making it customised for the role you're applying to.

All the best! <3

top_matched_solutions.parent_context:
1. How is the hostel, Mess(Food) and overall staying facility there??

2. The batch is small 90 each so how are the interaction with Professor, mere hisab se kafi high hona chahiye

3. Profs Dedicated Tech wale hai ya Managemennt wale hi Tech pada rahe hai??

top_matched_solutions.evidence_text:
# 1. Hostel, Mess (Food), and Staying Facilities

The staying facilities are quite comfortable. The mess food is decent, and they actually offer a pretty good menu. For accommodation, you get double sharing rooms, and you are paired with a student from your own course.

# 2. Interaction with Professors

Since the batch size is small (around 90 students per batch), the interaction with professors is very high, just as you'd expect. It is quite easy to approach, meet, and interact with the faculty members whenever needed.

# 3. Faculty (Tech vs. Management)

The faculty lineup is a balanced mix. There are dedicated tech professors as well as management professors, so you get the right expertise for both technical and business subjects rather than management faculty trying to teach core tech.

# 4. Coding and Placement Culture

The coding culture is still growing. Honestly, only a few people are heavily into core coding right now—myself and one of my friends are actively doing it and focusing on platforms like LeetCode and Kaggle. A good portion of the batch isn't as intensely focused on it yet.

# 5. Education Loan Process & Campus Banks

Yes, education loan facilities are readily available. Union Bank of India has a presence here to assist students. You don't necessarily have to get it done beforehand from home; you can easily get your loan processed through the bank branches that visit the campus during the orientation program. You just need to bring your official offer letter along.
